rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (score 893.6, best so far): the oval finishes 20/20 at 2.04 s, the s-bend finishes 20/20 at 2.25 s, and the slalom finishes 15/20. The five slalom failures all end off track, and the slalom minimum score of 170 shows these runs fail late. Steering oscillation (0.25) and rms error (0.012 m) on the slalom are low, so the loop is stable. The remaining loss is off-track drift on the sharpest bends at base_speed 1.2. Expected value: each slalom failure costs roughly 700 points, and a 25% failure rate costs about 175 points on average. Change: base_speed 1.2 -> 1.1, a single-variable change. Geometry and gains stay as in iteration 3 so the effect is readable. Trade-off: completion time rises by roughly 0.1 to 0.2 s per track, which costs only about 2 to 4 points per run in the time term. Hypotheses: (H1) at 1.1 the slalom off-track rate falls from 25% to under 10%, raising the slalom mean above 900; (H2) oval and s-bend stay at 100% and 95 to 100% finish, with completion_time under 2.5 s on the slalom; (H3) if slalom failures persist at 1.1, the cause is not speed, and the next step is a sensor-spread or kd change, not a further speed cut. Measurements wanted per track: completion, completion_time, progress, line_loss_events, max_error, and steering_oscillation, to confirm whether off-track events now come from line loss or from overshoot.
